congo-brazzaville-oil-seizures-debt-fund.whole: In December 2007 Congo swapped about US$2.3 billion of London Club bank claims (US$300 million of principal plus about US$2 billion of interest arrears built up since 1984) for US$477.8 million in new bonds due 2029; over 92% of creditors took part, according to Cleary Gottlieb, which represented Congo in the deal. In January 2010 the IMF and the World Bank's IDA announced debt-service savings of US$1.9 billion for Congo (about US$1.7 billion under the HIPC debt-relief scheme and about US$201 million under MDRI), by their own count. These figures come from Congo's own legal adviser and the lenders; no independent check was found.

marrakech-agadir-motorway-blasting.whole: The Marrakech–Agadir motorway opened on 21 June 2010 at a cost of 8 billion dirhams, cutting the trip to about 2 hours from an average of four (Bladi.net, 2008 and 2010); traffic was expected to average about 4,000 vehicles a day, 40% of them heavy trucks (Bladi.net). In 2004 the operator ADM had projected 7,000 to 7,460 vehicles a day by 2015, on a then-estimated cost of 6.2 billion dirhams (La Vie éco). Japan's aid agency JICA, which financed a different 46 km section (Argana–Ameskroud), reported traffic there rising from 3,219 vehicles a day in 2010 to 6,621 in 2013, against a target of 6,396, and rated its loan 'highly satisfactory'. No AfDB completion evaluation and no independent check were found.

senegal-senelec-privatisation.whole: The World Bank's own completion report rated the credit's outcome as unsatisfactory ('marginally unsatisfactory' in its text) and its sustainability 'unlikely'. The petroleum part went furthest: a US$2.30 per barrel refinery surcharge was removed and subsidies on cooking gas (LPG) and power-station fuel were abolished. In power, a regulator (CRSE) was created but had 'little real effect' because Senelec stayed state-run; generation capacity grew through a private power plant and power from the Manantali dam. The consortium bid 27.83 euros a share for 34% of Senelec, and the Bank released a third tranche (SDR 33.5 million) in December 2001 after a second buyer was named; that sale was declared unsuccessful in 2002. These are the Bank's own assessments; no independent check was found.

zambia-2022-fuel-subsidy-removal.whole: By the IMF's count at the programme's final review (January 2026), Zambia drew SDR 1,271.66 million (about US$1.7 billion). Year-end inflation was 16.7% in 2024 and was projected at 8.2% for 2025; the cash budget deficit narrowed from 8.1% of GDP in 2021 to an estimated 3.5% in 2024; and public debt, estimated at 101.8% of GDP in 2024, was projected to fall to 68.5% in 2027, with deals with commercial creditors not yet complete. A missed reserve target at end-June 2025 needed an IMF waiver. These are the IMF's own figures; no independent check was found.

greece-health-spending-cap.whole: Public health spending in Greece fell by €5.2 billion between 2009 and 2013, a 32% drop in real terms, and the state's medicines bill fell by €1.8 billion, mainly through price cuts and generics; it was still about 1.9% of GDP, the highest in the OECD (OECD, 2016). From June 2014 uninsured people were covered for prescribed medicines and public hospital emergency care (OECD). The European Court of Auditors found the bailout programmes met their aims 'only to a limited extent': the underlying budget balance improved by 17% of GDP over 2009-2015, while debt as a share of GDP kept rising.

indonesia-palm-oil-export-ban-1998.whole: In 1998, the year of the export ban and the high export taxes that replaced it, crude palm oil exports fell 27%, from 3 million tonnes in 1997 to 2.2 million, and palm oil export earnings fell 48%, from US$1.4 billion to US$745 million; CIFOR estimates the ban and taxes cost Indonesia about US$1 billion in export earnings that year. Domestic cooking oil cost Rp 5,900/kg in July 1998, against Rp 1,750/kg a year earlier. New planting dropped: the government expected 177,197 ha to be planted in 1999, down 33% from 266,565 ha in 1997 (CIFOR).

luanshya-ramcoz-sale.whole: The Binani Group paid US$35 million for Roan Antelope Copper Mines (RAMCOZ) in 1997, took over 6,200 workers and agreed not to retrench for two years; RAMCOZ went into receivership in 2000, and in 2004 the government released US$35 million for former workers' terminal benefits (Deputy Finance Minister's answer to parliament, via Zambian Observer). John Perry's account (summarised by The Violence of Development) says about 30% of power was still lost, half the population still had no grid connection, and cuts lasted up to ten hours a day in 2006-2007. mexico-1982-imf-subsidy-wage-cuts.whole: The programme aimed to close a public-sector deficit of 18% of GDP in 1982. After the November 1982 IMF accord, Mexico negotiated a US$10 billion rescue package with private banks; the 1983 measures eliminated both the fiscal and trade deficits, but through sharply reduced imports and a severe recession, and inflation did not fall significantly. After the IMF suspended disbursements in September 1985, growth slowed and inflation surged (Library of Congress). A 1986 agreement brought about US$12.5 billion in new private and official credit.

nigeria-power-tariff-2020.whole: By the World Bank's count, tariff shortfalls (the gap the government pays to cover below-cost tariffs) fell 71%, from ₦581 billion in 2019 to ₦166 billion in 2022 (World Bank project paper, 2023); Nairametrics also reports regulatory cost recovery rising from 56% to 94%, and quotes a Bank note that early results were 'achieved and verified'. bolivia-pension-privatization.whole: A background paper for the World Bank's evaluation office (by economist Salvador Valdés-Prieto) reported that contributors rose from about 300,000 in 1995 to about 450,000 in 2001, pension fund investments reached US$1.1 billion (14% of GDP), returns were 7-8% a year in dollars in 2001-2002, and the Bonosol paid about 340,000 elderly people a year in 1997-2000; it also found the reform raised the pension-related budget deficit from 0.2% to 5.0% of GDP (reached in 2002). The ILO gives a different picture: coverage stayed around 12% of the labour force from 1997 to 2009, transition costs were 2.5 times the first projections, and pensions averaged 20% of past average salary.

serbia-2014-pension-wage-cuts.whole: By the IMF's own count, the general government deficit went from about 6.6% of GDP in 2014 to a projected surplus of 0.2% in 2017, and public debt fell from a peak of about 76% of GDP around 2015 to 65.4% at end-September 2017; the wage bill fell from 10% of GDP in 2014 to about 8.3%, and the pension bill from 13% to about 11.4%. The IMF said the arrangement 'succeeded in addressing large macroeconomic imbalances'; no independent check of these figures was found. In October 2018 the IMF reported the temporary pension cuts would be reversed from November 2018 and debt was projected below 55% of GDP by end-2018.

barbados-2018-public-sector-layoffs.whole: A US Treasury report to Congress, drawing on IMF data, gives public debt as 157% of GDP when the IMF programme was approved in 2018 (it also says 'around 160%'), falling after domestic (October 2018) and external (December 2019) debt restructurings to 122% in March 2020 (the same report gives 125% for the end of the 2019/20 fiscal year), then rising to 142% in the pandemic as nominal GDP fell 17%. The Treasury says Barbados delivered the targeted 6% of GDP primary surplus in 2019, then ran primary deficits of 1% of GDP in 2020 and 2021, and that reserves rose from about three to about eight months of imports by October 2021. The IMF says reserves rose from about US$220 million in May 2018 to about US$1.5 billion by June 2022, and the economy shrank 14% in 2020. These are IMF and US government figures; no independent check was found.

romania-social-dialogue-act-2011.whole: The 2011 programme was precautionary; Romania drew none of the money, and the IMF closed its final reviews in June 2013 (Romania Insider; bne IntelliNews). The European Commission reported GDP growth of 2.5% in 2011 after a fall of more than 8% in 2009–10, and a deficit of 5.2% of GDP in 2011 on an accrual basis (4.1% on a cash basis). In October 2012 Commission and IMF staff called Law 62/2011 'a key reform' for labour relations but gave no figures on its effects. Trif and Paolucci report that the number of workers on the minimum wage almost quadrupled from 2011 to 2016, and that about three million people emigrated over 25 years, over half since 2008, which kept unemployment fairly low.

An unpublished independent audit reported by The Guardian via Nairametrics (2016) found terminal operators invested over N200 billion in 2006–2015 and channel dredging raised the draft from about 7 to 13.5 metres, but said the Nigerian Ports Authority had only partly met its own obligations on power, road and rail access.

kazakhstan-pension-privatization.whole: The ADB's completion report (2000) rated its loan 'partly successful': by March 2000 about 3.1 million people contributed to the funded accounts, assets reached T70.4 billion (3.6% of 1999 GDP), and pension arrears, about T40 billion at the start of 1997, were cleared in 1997 and again in early 2000 after they built up again. An evaluation paper for the World Bank's evaluators (Palmer) found assets grew from 4.3% of GDP in 2000 to 7.2% in 2002, and participation from 20% of the labour force in 1998 to almost 75% by 2002; it also found that in 2003 government bonds returned 6.2–6.5% against 6.8% inflation, and 13 of 16 private funds reported negative returns. Pensions have been paid on time since 2002 (Palmer).

nicaragua-esaf-public-pay-freeze.whole: IMF figures show growth averaging about 4.5% a year in 1994–98, end-year inflation falling from 12.4% in 1994 to 7.3% in 1997 (18.5% in 1998 after Hurricane Mitch), and the deficit after grants falling from 7.9% to 3.3% of GDP; external debt fell from 638% of GDP in 1994 to 280% in 1998, and the IMF still judged it unsustainable. Acevedo (Envío) reports that the part of foreign debt service paid from national resources took an average 51% of fiscal income in 1994–98, that the IMF suspended the second ESAF in 2001 when the deficit rose, and that after HIPC debt relief in 2004 debt service fell to US$87 million in 2005, under 9% of fiscal income.

kharkiv-metro-extension-compensation.whole: Nothing has been delivered yet. The EIB's 2017 loan was for a 3.5 km extension with two stations, a depot and 17 five-car trains, to serve a southern area then reached only by trolleybuses, buses and minibuses, with completion expected by end-2023.
